relevanz: Re-runs the non-native-speaker detector bias test on newer models, turning a single 2023 finding into a time series — the shape an argument needs to claim a bias persists rather than merely occurred once.
Measures LLM use across the literature without a detector, by tracking excess vocabulary — a design that sidesteps the very detector-bias problem other entries here document.
The peer-reviewed statement of model collapse the self-consumption work argues from — Nature rather than preprint, which is the difference when a claim has to bear weight.
The original finding that detectors misclassify non-native writers — the baseline without which the 2026 re-test elsewhere in this catalogue would state nothing.
Names cognitive injustice: the failure to recognise other ways of knowing. A frame for asking what a machine-run research practice excludes by construction rather than by choice.
Argues that making is itself a form of knowing, across anthropology, archaeology, art and architecture — the premise on which research through practice rests at all.
A field survey with a working definition of machine creativity — useful less as theory than as a limit on what a machine-run practice may claim about its own output.
A handbook account of practice-led research, structured like a doctoral programme — the methodological grammar of research-through-practice, spelled out.
Defines benchmark saturation and measures it across 60 benchmarks — a quantified account of measuring instruments losing their power to discriminate, which is the field's own subject.
Formalises a case where two provenance defences (C2PA and watermarking) authenticate contradictory claims — a verification failure produced by combining verifiers, not by either one failing.
Tests three common detectors and puts a number on the trade between accuracy and fairness — the measured version of the claim that detection accuracy is bought with bias.
Documents systematic distortion in Chatbot Arena rankings — an audit of the instrument everyone treats as authoritative, and so a model case of a measurement becoming the object.
Asks what harm detection models do when they are wrong, not only how often they are right — the consequence side that an accuracy figure alone conceals.
Measures narrowing linguistic diversity under LLM use — the same contraction the model-collapse literature predicts for model outputs, observed here in human writing instead.
A benchmark rebuilt to exclude training-data contamination — the concrete remedy to the problem that otherwise makes saturation findings unreadable.
Quantifies how far simple evasion pushes detector accuracy below its already low 39.5% — the robustness figure any claim about detectability has to survive.
Estimates LLM share at corpus level without classifying individual texts — a measurement design that engineers around per-document detection error instead of lamenting it.
The journal version of the evasion study, aimed at education — where a detector's output has immediate consequences for a named individual.
A candid account of non-response when surveying officials — method material for the case where the object of a measurement can decline to be measured.
Shows a fraud-detection method producing false findings when misapplied to dichotomous variables — a verification instrument turning into a source of error through misuse.
The original MMLU benchmark — the instrument whose saturation and contamination the other entries in this catalogue go on to measure.
Documents terminal-digit bias in clinical blood-pressure readings — human rounding as a measurable artefact, and a clean comparison case precisely because it is far from AI.
Quantifies when Gaia parallaxes with poor astrometric fits remain usable — the reliability question sitting underneath the parallax work.
The nearby-star catalogue the parallax work builds on — and one of the few holdings that state their own completeness in figures rather than in prose.
Provides a way to recognise unreliable Gaia solutions BEFORE analysis — the exclusion step without which a parallax measurement would rest on artefacts.
A validated binary-star catalogue that ships a chance-alignment probability for every pair — a dataset that carries its own error rate instead of leaving it to the user.
Sets out why inverting a parallax yields wrong distances and what to do instead — the inference problem the negative-parallax work turns on.
